speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me how long this has been going on and if you notice any redness or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gamekeeper's Thumb (Ulnar Collateral Ligament Injury of the MCP Joint). The mechanism of injury (forced abduction of the finger) and the specific finger involved strongly suggest an injury to the ulnar collateral ligament, often referred to as a "skier's thumb" when occurring at the thumb, but the description of a finger caught in a jersey and pulled suggests a similar mechanism affecting the ring finger's PIP joint or a specific laceration of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon (hitchhiker thumb mechanism). Given the "pulled away forcefully" mechanism, a rupture of the ulnar collateral ligament at the PIP joint of the ring finger is the most likely diagnosis, though a flexor digitorum profundus rupture is also possible. I will request imaging to confirm the specific structure involved. REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray of right hand (AP and lateral views) to rule out avulsion fracture.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
